checks.issue: A COLOPHON AT LAST, AND IT IS THE FIRST IN THIS WHOLE STRETCH. มังคะละสุตตัง นิฏฐิตัง. is printed CENTRED under verse 28, so it goes in as the chant's `closing` rather than as a verse. Every chant since page 64 has had the `closing` key left off because the book printed none — this is the first that prints one, which is worth recording because the absence had started to look like a rule.

A CANONICAL CITATION CARRYING TWO REFERENCES. The superscript 1 sits on this verse and the footnote reads ขุ. ขุ. 25/3 ขุ. สุ. 25/376 — the Khuddakapāṭha and the Suttanipāta, both printings of the same sutta. Reproduced verbatim as one string, neither split nor expanded, because that is how the book sets it.

มังคะละมุตตะมันติ. carries the quotative ติ closing the deity's whole question and the Buddha's whole answer, where the other nine refrains end plainly มังคะละมุตตะมัง. — so the last one is marked as the end of a quotation. Read at 2.2x. Reproduced, and romanised muttamanti to match.

TWO COLUMNS, gutter measured at x 940-1160 — a different position from page 81's x 1080, on the same chant. The metre is the same; the setting simply shifts across the page turn. Measured rather than carried over.

checks.issue: THE PAGE AND THE CONTENTS SPACE THIS TITLE DIFFERENTLY. The page heading prints บทขัด ระตะนะสุตตัง with a SPACE after บทขัด; the book's own สารบัญ lists บทขัดระตะนะสุตตัง with none. The page is reproduced. The romanisation is unaffected by the space so the contents' value is used unchanged, but note the same consequence as page 80: because title_thai is no longer a key in _CONTENTS_ROMAN, the never-spell-a-title-two-ways test cannot see this chant. Second title in three pages where that is true.

SET BOTH WAYS, and both groups declare their layout. Eight lines of justified prose (ink x 300-1820, no gutter anywhere) then four two-column rows (gutter x 960-1140). Verse 1 carries para_layout 'prose' and verse 13 'lines'; neither relies on the chant default. Same shape as page 81's sutta.

A HYPHEN ACROSS THE GUTTER, the second in four pages after page 79's สัมมา-. The left column ends โรคามะนุสสะทุพภิกขะ- and the right column opens สัมภูตันติวิธัมภะยัง, so the word is rejoined as โรคามะนุสสะทุพภิกขะสัมภูตันติวิธัมภะยัง and the hyphen dropped as typesetting. It also settles the two-column reading of this block on its own, independently of the measured gutter.

A WIDE GAP INSIDE LINE 2 OF THE PROSE, between ทะสะ and ปะระมัตถะปาระมิโย — visibly wider than the other word spaces on that line. Read as JUSTIFICATION rather than as meaningful spacing, and set as a single space here. Worth an eye at the book, since the rule elsewhere is to reproduce unusual spacing.

จักกะวาเฬสุ IS ฬ, the third instance in four pages, and the same test settles it: the letter carries a tall ascender that the พ elsewhere on the sheet lack. ยัสสาณัมปะฏิคคัณหันติ at verse 14 is BARE, with no mark over the ณ, consistent with pages 68 to 76.

english_unverified is set, and this chant's English is the least certain on the page. The prose preface is a single compressed sentence listing the Buddha's perfections and deeds in the accusative before its verb arrives twelve units later; the gloss keeps the list order the book prints and does not try to smooth the syntax. Worth reading against the book.

batch_status.notes: THREE CHANTS AND THREE DIFFERENT SETTINGS ON ONE SHEET — two-column, prose-then-two-column, and centred single column. Profiling each block separately is the only reason all three were read correctly, and this is the third page running where that has mattered. Four things for Josh. (1) THE FIRST COLOPHON IN THIS WHOLE STRETCH: มังคะละสุตตัง นิฏฐิตัง. is printed centred under the sutta, so that chant takes a `closing` at last — every chant since page 64 has had the key left off because the book printed none, and the absence had begun to look like a rule. (2) A CITATION WITH TWO REFERENCES, ขุ. ขุ. 25/3 ขุ. สุ. 25/376, reproduced verbatim as one string. (3) A SECOND HYPHEN ACROSS A GUTTER, after page 79's, settling that block's two-column reading on its own. (4) THE PAGE SPACES A TITLE DIFFERENTLY FROM THE CONTENTS — บทขัด ระตะนะสุตตัง against บทขัดระตะนะสุตตัง — which is the second title in three pages the contents test can no longer see. Nothing on this page needs re-photographing.
diacritic_exceptions: va/vā — genuinely two different words, and the BOOK prints the difference. Verse 2 of ratana-suttam-dutiyam reads ภุมมานิ วา with the long วา, the disjunctive 'or', separating beings of the earth from beings of the sky. Verse 3 reads สัพเพ วะ ภูตา with the short วะ, the emphatic particle eva reduced, meaning 'all beings indeed'. Long against short is visible in the Thai on two consecutive printed lines, so making them agree would erase a distinction the page makes and change the sense of one of them.
